analysis: Both changed files are test-only. The single changed line in each (StandaloneServerModelAdmissionTests.swift:20 and StandaloneServerTests.swift:663) updates a stub LanguageModel's prepare signature from (windowSize: Int?) to (state: LMOutput.State?, prefill: PrefillParameters). This tracks an upstream MLXLMCommon protocol change, presumably a dependency bump that is not in the supplied evidence. The stubs return .tokens(input.text) and newCache returns [], so no weights load and no inference runs. Nothing touches the production code paths covered by the threat model: coordinator WebSocket, attestation, key custody, encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041), fan helper, App Attest. The head-text of StandaloneServerModelAdmissionTests.swift is entirely test scaffolding with inert engines and hooks, and it does not alter any security control. It exercises model admission, eviction, the local-mode 404 and 429 error envelopes that do not reflect request-derived model ids, and weight-hash trimming. The StandaloneServerTests.swift base text asserts bearer-token enforcement, the 32 MiB body limit and the fixed error envelope; these tests are unchanged apart from the stub signature. Remaining question for integration: whether the production code and the dependency bump that motivated the signature change are reviewed elsewhere, since they are outside this batch. No security regression identified in these units.
